about: Test vectors for the watch rules in WatchRules.kt, run by the Kotlin tests and by the Swift port. A case runs on a feed (named in feeds) at a time now, in epoch seconds, and gives what each rule answers there: next and previous as prayer, at and dayIndex; secondsLeft; progress, held to within tolerance.progress; countdown; and the row lit on the Prayer screen's rule (litOnList) and on the widgets' (litOnGlance). Where the rules have no moment, next, previous, secondsLeft, progress and countdown are null: before the feed's first start, and at and after its last. next and previous are the phone's own: for the day now is on, yesterday's starts that come before today's Fajr and all five of today's, so that a start falling after the next day's Fajr is counted to until midnight and dropped once the date has turned (tromso-late-maghrib); of two starts on one instant the earlier prayer is next and the later previous (capetown-combined-maghrib-isha). The row lit is today's. A day runs from its own midnight (the midnight field of the day, in epoch seconds) to the next day's, and a day whose midnight is 0 begins at solar midnight instead, halfway between its Dhuhr and the day before's (todayIndex in WatchRules.kt; capetown-no-midnights). Numbers the watch writes use the nine digits that follow ui.digitZero (capetown-ar-sa, capetown-bn, capetown-ur). countdowns are countdown on its own, and refreshes are needsRefresh. VectorsTest.kt writes this file and checks it, and nobody edits it: change the rules, then rewrite it with ./gradlew :watchcore:testAndroidHostTest -Ptaqwa.updateVectors and commit the result.
